rendered: No. The document does not compare the sensor against PCR or blood culture on the clinical samples. The clinical part uses serum from enrolled subjects: septic patients with confirmed E. coli infection, septic patients with confirmed E. faecium infection, and healthy volunteers as controls ("[1]"). Discrimination of these serum groups is shown by LDA score plots (Fig. 5c[2]). PCR and bacterial culture appear only in the introduction, as techniques widely used for pathogen identification that are time-consuming and need specialized expertise: "[3]". The standard plate count was used only to set the viable cell concentration of the laboratory bacterial strains, not as a comparison method for the clinical samples: "[4]" count. No PCR or blood culture results for the patient samples are reported.
